output.subject: We have received your complaint about your homeowners insurance premium
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for contacting us, and for taking the time to explain what has happened. We understand how worrying this situation must be, and we're sorry for the stress and frustration it has caused.

We have received your complaint. Here is our understanding of what you told us:

- You received a cancellation notice from your homeowners insurance carrier saying that your $2,184 premium had not been paid from your escrow account.
- You mentioned that the policy is due to cancel on 9/29.
- You told us you called us on 9/18 and were told the matter would be escalated, but you did not see any action afterwards.
- When you spoke with us again, you were told the carrier information we hold may be out of date.
- You asked us to confirm the position in writing.

A specialist team is now reviewing your complaint and will respond to you within 10 business days. If you have any further correspondence from your insurance carrier, please keep it, as it may help with the review.

Thank you again for bringing this to our attention.

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Policy cancels 9/29; the 10-business-day response window may run past that date, so consider whether faster contact is needed.
Check the status of the rush disbursement the representative submitted and whether the carrier has received payment.
Decide whether to tell the customer about the rush disbursement; the draft does not mention it.
Verify and update the carrier information on file.
Review what happened after the 9/18 call and why the escalation was not acted on.
Customer requested written confirmation of the disbursement; decide what to provide and when.
Consider whether the customer needs anything to show the carrier to prevent or reverse the cancellation.
